summary: Round 1 review of SuspiciousAlignment/Projected/LossThreshold.lean: ACCEPT (no blocker, no major issue; 6 minor). Soundness: `scripts/leancheck` on the file exits 0 with no output (no errors, no warnings, about 20 s); grep finds no sorry/admit/axiom/native_decide/unsafe/implemented_by (one kernel `decide` for spec2.B = {1}); the module builds; `#print axioms` on all 140 declarations (scratch Axioms.lean) reports only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. Imports are Mathlib and SuspiciousAlignment.Defs only; no Defs quantity is redefined (LossThreshold.root is definitionally the Defs formula for thetaCrit); no fully-qualified name clash with the other 11 project files. Fidelity: every statement in scope (eq. (3)-(5), Theorem 10 with pathwise identity, per-coordinate sum and both sign characterisations, the 'Additional Notion', both appendix lemmas, Theorem 11 with uniqueness of the root in (0,1) and all three orderings, the Summary consequence) has a Lean counterpart that says what the paper says, with the extra hypotheses (0 < tau^S + n^loss_S; s^D, s^B > 0; n^loss_D, n^loss_B > 0) explicit in the statements and documented. No main theorem exploits x/0 = 0 or sqrt of a negative number, hypotheses are jointly satisfiable (concrete Lean instances, reproduced in python), and elaborated types are all real-valued. Independent numerics: Theorem 10 on 20000 random instances and Theorem 11 plus the critical-root lemma and the Summary consequence on 50000 random interior instances gave 0 violations. Fidelity note: honest and essentially complete. I verified its claims independently: the paper only assumes Sigma PSD with positive trace (tex 353, 380), so n^loss_D > 0 and n^loss_B > 0 are genuine extra assumptions (counterexamples kap2 = (0,5) -> thetaCrit = 0 and kap2 = (1,0) -> thetaCrit = 1 confirmed); alpha_t > 0 fails or is undefined off 0 < theta_t < 1; thetaCrit is state dependent (same theta = 0.8, opposite orderings at c = (1,1) and (1/2,1/2)); the typos at tex 1477, 1544, 1690, 1694, 1709 are real; the out-of-scope warning that the lower bound of Theorem 13 is false is confirmed numerically (1 - thetaCrit = 0.00109 < 1/114). Minor points: the note's 'no theorem uses x/0 = 0' holds for main theorems but not for a few helper lemmas; proof-internal claims of the critical-root lemma (strict discriminant, negative second root) and the raw quotient identity of tex 1690 are not separate statements; boundary states theta_t in {0,1} have no statement although the ordering there is convention-free and the note's '(0, thetaCrit)' correction is slightly too strong; a gap1 = lam_{k+1}(m-1) bridging lemma for the next file is missing; three docstrings overstate.
